candidates.title: Proton-readout correlation set
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA versus TEOA selectivity differences in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system track directly measured bulk proton-management and medium descriptors rather than composition labels alone.
candidates.source_to_proposal: Sources indicate that TEOA-containing systems can change proton availability, dissolved CO2-related behavior, conductivity, viscosity, and other medium properties, and that proton-transfer environments can be mechanistically discriminated in other cobalt systems. The proposal transfers only the idea of measuring donor-dependent covariates alongside catalysis in the same baseline formulation; it does not assume the same mechanism or any specific magnitude/direction in Co-bpy.

comparisons.inference: Primary descriptive comparison: if CO/H2 and bulk proton/medium descriptors differ together under otherwise matched conditions, the donor effect is at least consistent with changed proton-management or medium environment, but not proven causal.

Within TEOA, isotope-sensitive changes test whether measured descriptors and product distribution respond to proton-transfer perturbation; any effect remains a combined proton-transfer and solvent-isotope perturbation.
Within TEA, isotope-sensitive changes provide the corresponding proton-transfer-sensitive comparison for the alternative amine environment.

TEOA versus TEA under deuterated medium tests whether donor-dependent differences persist after a matched isotope perturbation; persistence would weaken a simple proton-management-only account, while collapse would support it descriptively.

procedure: Prepare the four matched formulations from one verified P01 stock plan, changing only amine identity and water isotope while keeping reactor geometry, gas handling, illumination, and sampling times identical.

Before irradiation, equilibrate each sample with CO2 using the same handling routine, then record bulk descriptors feasible in the medium: pH or pD proxy, conductivity, and a standardized CO2 uptake-related equilibration measure.
Run the matched photocatalytic test and quantify both CO and H2 with the same analytical method, while repeating the same bulk-descriptor measurements after irradiation.
Compare donor-dependent product outputs with donor-dependent descriptor values and descriptor changes, emphasizing paired contrasts rather than pooled correlations.
measurements: CO amount or rate under each group
H2 amount or rate under each group
CO/H2 product ratio or selectivity descriptor
Pre-irradiation pH proxy for H2O media or pD proxy for D2O media
Post-irradiation pH or pD proxy shift
A standardized CO2 uptake-relevant equilibration readout such as pressure-drop or mass-change proxy if technically valid in the chosen reactor
Replicate-to-replicate variation of each bulk descriptor
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible association in which TEA and TEOA show different CO/H2 behavior together with different bulk proton/medium descriptors, and donor-dependent selectivity differences weaken or change under the matched D2O perturbation. This would support a medium/proton-management contribution, while still not excluding parallel redox or cobalt-state effects.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 as the main explanation would be that TEA and TEOA give clearly different CO/H2 outputs while the measured proton/medium descriptors are indistinguishable within uncertainty and the isotope perturbation leaves the donor contrast essentially unchanged. That outcome would favor explanations centered elsewhere, such as donor redox chemistry or cobalt-state formation.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if catalytic differences are not reproducible, if bulk descriptor measurements are unstable or not interpretable in the mixed medium, if D2O changes multiple properties without a consistent pattern, or if descriptors differ but do not track product behavior across matched repeats. Bulk correlation alone cannot assign microscopic intermediates or prove local interfacial conditions.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-anchored P01 formulation as the starting recipe and verify any missing numerical settings from the supplied source before execution. If exact pH/pD metrology is unreliable in the mixed solvent, run a pilot to choose one calibrated proxy method and use it consistently for all groups rather than mixing scales. Pilot-test conductivity range, CO2 equilibration time, and sampling timing on non-catalytic blanks or duplicate baseline mixtures until readings stabilize and do not disturb the catalytic run. If the D2O substitution materially alters miscibility or instrument response, document that as a transfer limit and treat isotope comparisons as bounded descriptive tests.
candidates.limitations: This is a bounded correlation experiment, not a single-factor causal proof of proton management. TEA and TEOA may also alter quenching, coordination, viscosity, and CO2 solvation simultaneously. Bulk pH/pD and conductivity do not establish the local environment at cobalt sites or on g-C3N4, and isotope substitution changes more than proton-transfer kinetics. A CO2 uptake proxy may be reactor-specific and can suggest, but not prove, amine-CO2 adduct chemistry.
